regions.merged_text: He who stiffneckedly persists in his opinion, says St. John Climeceus, even when he's in the right, will be fired on by satan. Beware of "die Genuss, Hab= & Ehrsucht, " as the tripple enemy of the soul. "Love Him who is the first cause of so many beautiful creations" - To St. Augustine con- sidering the beauties of the fields. Means of Increasing Desires of Perfection 1. Meditation: 2. Renewal frequently of resolve to strive for Love of God - to be grateful to Jesus, i.e. to resolve on becoming perfect, as the just beginning; 3rd. Never dwell in thought on the good we have done but on the contrary (while remembering our sins past) look to the good yet to be accomplished. Scaramelli P. 70

regions.merged_text: "As for desiring to do things which may deserve glory, though it is what magnanimity desires, yet the magnanimus man desires it not for the glory that arises therefrom but only that he may deserve the glory without possessing it. On the contrary he has raised himself so high above the opinion of the world, that finding nothing estimable but virtue & looking with the same eye on the praise and scorn of men, he does nothing for love of the one or through fear of the other. He makes no account of worldly honors; his flight is higher. - it is for love of God and virtue that he is moved to perform great actions; all other motives have no influence on him. Virtue is so excellent a thing that men cannot eather reward or recompense it sufficiently. God alone can do this."
